$comment: PURPOSE AND SHAPE: One note per top-level CIS Control (18 of them), the parent tier above the safeguards emitted by the companion cis-controls-v8-flat recipe. PROPERTIES: title (the control's short name), control (the control number, and the join key the safeguard notes point back at via their own control property), and level (a literal 'control' discriminator, because both tiers come from the same sheet and may land in one vault). curie is emitted automatically from source.ontology plus the identifier and is deliberately not declared here. BODY: the source's Description column is the control's normative statement (109 to 497 characters across the 18 rows) and is projected as a single '## Control' section. It was previously a frontmatter value; moving it is the point of this revision. PROPERTIES-VS-BODY RATIONALE: a multi-sentence normative paragraph in YAML is unreadable in Obsidian's property panel, awkward to escape, and invisible to body search; identity and short discriminators are the opposite and stay in frontmatter where Bases can tabulate them and the Tier 2 projection can index them. No H1 is emitted: Obsidian already renders the note title, so a heading that repeats the identifier or the title is noise. SOURCE NOTE: on the control rows the CIS Control cell is inconsistently typed — some are numbers, some are strings with a trailing space ('1 ') — hence the trim filter in both the layout template and the managed property; without it the filename would keep the trailing space. RIGHTS — RESTRICTED: CIS Controls v8.1.2 is published under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International, and its workbook stays local-only under the gitignored Frameworks/ corpus. This recipe is a method — column names, templates, and section headings, containing no CIS content — so the recipe file itself may be committed. Generated notes, sample output, screenshots showing CIS content, and any excerpt of CIS Description or Title text MUST NOT be committed or published. Corpus provenance and rights posture: https://cybersader.github.io/crosswalker/reference/framework-corpus/. KNOWN GAP 1 — the control-to-child-safeguards relationship is not emitted at all. The children are separate rows in the same sheet, and a flat file layout with no cross-recipe relationship projection cannot gather them (source.where selects which rows become notes, it does not gather one note's children); target.enrichment children lists work within one import batch, and these two tiers are two separate imports. Emitting a guessed link set would be worse than emitting none. ROW SELECTION (SchemaVer 1.9.0 — this replaces what was KNOWN GAP 2, which said no row predicate existed) — the workbook keeps control rows and safeguard rows in ONE sheet, distinguished only by whether CIS Safeguard is blank. source.where is "$trim(`CIS Safeguard`) = ''", which admits the 18 control rows and excludes the 153 safeguard rows; the companion cis-controls-v8-flat recipe declares the exact opposite predicate over the same sheet. Verified against the shipped export: 'Controls v8.1.2' yields 171 data rows, 18 with a strictly empty CIS Safeguard and 153 non-empty. Neither recipe needs a pre-filtered row selection any more — both can be pointed at that sheet as shipped. The pair still exists because the two tiers are two different answers to 'what is a row', and that difference is now stated in the recipes rather than in an undocumented manual preprocessing step. $trim matters on this polarity: the same sheet types some control-row cells with a trailing space, which is why the layout template and the managed property already trim. A mistyped column name is refused at preflight rather than silently admitting zero rows.
